parts.text: A student investigates the resistances of combinations of resistors. The first circuit arrangement is shown in Fig. 2.1. Fig. 2.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) The student measures the current and decides to use a lower current. He adds a variable resistor to the circuit to reduce the current. On Fig. 2.1, mark with an X a suitable position in the circuit for the variable resistor. [1] Fig. 2.2 Fig. 2.3

ms.label: 2(a)
ms.text: X marked anywhere in the series circuit

parts.label: i
parts.text: (b) (i) The student measures the current I 1 in the circuit. Record the current shown in Fig. 2.2. I 1 = .......................................................A [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) He measures the potential difference (p.d.) V 1 across resistors R A and R B in series. Record the potential difference V 1 shown in Fig. 2.3. V 1 = .......................................................V [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Calculate the resistance R 1 of the combination of resistors in series. Use the equation R 1 = V 1 I 1 . Include the unit. R 1 = ......................................................... [1]

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) The student connects a resistor R C in parallel with resistors R A and R B . He does not change the series combination of resistors R A and R B . He connects the voltmeter across the combination of all three resistors.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Draw a circuit diagram showing the circuit described in (d) . [2]

ms.label: 2(d)(i)
ms.text:
RC in parallel with resistors in series
voltmeter across candidate’s combination AND the rest of the circuit correct

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) The student measures the current I 2 in the circuit. 0.68 I 2 = ............................................................ A He measures the potential difference V 2 across the combination of the three resistors. 2.1 V 2 = ............................................................ V Calculate the resistance R 2 of the combination of resistors. Use the equation R 2 = V 2 I 2 . Include the unit. R 2 = ......................................................... [1]

ms.label: 2(d)(ii)
ms.text: 3.09 with unit Ω seen at least once in (c) (d) or (e) and not contradicted

parts.label: e
parts.text: (e) The student rearranges the resistors to set up the circuit shown in Fig. 2.4. Fig. 2.4 He measures the current I 3 in the circuit. 0.29 I 3 = ............................................................ A He measures the potential difference V 3 across the combination of the three resistors. 2.1 V 3 = ........................................................... V Calculate the resistance R 3 of the combination of resistors. Use the equation R 3 = V 3 I 3 . Include the unit. Give your answer to a suitable number of significant figures for this experiment. R 3 = ......................................................... [1]

parts.label: f
parts.text: (f) A student thinks the three resistors R A , R B and R C have the same resistance within the limits of experimental accuracy.

ms.label: 2(f)(i)
ms.text:
use of a voltmeter and/or an ammeter
measure V and I for each resistor and calculate R OR
connect each resistor to the same voltage supply and measure the current OR
connect resistors in series and measure the voltage across each of them OR
connect resistors in parallel and measure the current through them

ms.label: 2(f)(ii)
ms.text: check to see if the results are equal / close / within 10%
